top.title: New 49ers receiver Keenan Allen once beefed with Mike Evans on social media
top.description: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans speaks during a news conference following a win over the Seattle Seahawks in an NFL football game in Seattle, Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. (Lindsey Wasson/AP Photo/Lindsey Wasson) The San Francisco 49ers not only bolstered their receiving corps when they traded for Keenan Allen ahead of the trade deadline on Tuesday, they also reunited two former feuding players who got into it online. Back in 2020, a little less than four months after the NFL decided to move forward with a regularly scheduled season during the COVID-19 pandemic, Allen, then with the Chargers, took issue with the annual NFL Top 100 list of the league's best players. Specifically, he was incensed that he was placed at No. 77, so much so that he tweeted about it and tagged other players he thought he was better than: Tyreek Hill, Mike Evans and Chris Godwin. "Ok I'm tired of biten my tongue…@cheetah @MikeEvans13_ @chrisgoodwin… (and the list goes on) ARE NOT a better reciever than me! Faster than me…every day of the week but separation..CHILD PLEASE!" Allen wrote . It's not hard to see where Allen's frustrations were coming from as he was ranked No. 38 on the list the year before. He might have been so upset that he forgot to check that he tagged the correct Chris Godwin in his post (he did not). Regardless, Evans replied to the callout. "You tagged the wrong Chris Godwin lol and don't be mad at us we ain't make the rankings or care about em," Evans replied . "I like the confidence but be realistic you not on my level bro." You tagged the wrong Chris Godwin lol and don't be mad at us we ain't make the rankings or care about em. I like the confidence but be realistic you not on my level bro - Mike Evans (@MikeEvans13_) July 27, 2020 Allen did not respond, but did follow up his own post with , "IM THE BEST WR IN THE AFC WEST!!! Without question!!!" Statistically speaking, Evans came out on top at the end of that season. He finished with 1,006 yards and 13 touchdowns on 70 receptions as his Tom Brady-led Buccaneers team won the Super Bowl. Allen still had an incredible year, grabbing 100 receptions in 14 games for 992 yards and eight touchdowns. Six years is a long time for people to think about some Twitter beef that lasted all of two posts - and one side even conceding some respect for the other. Still, if both players could tap into the competitiveness that led to the kinds of seasons they respectively put together that year, then the Niners are in for one hell of a receiving duo. top.title: LASWA, Interferry complete ferry safety inspection training
top.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Waterways Authority (LASWA), in partnership with global trade association Interferry, has concluded Module 6 of the Africa Ferry Safety Development and Mentoring Programme to strengthen safety standards across the waterways sector. The training equipped maritime professionals with technical skills to audit and inspect commercial passenger ferries as part of efforts to improve passenger safety and compliance with international maritime standards. The module, titled “Survey and Inspection”, combined self-paced theoretical lessons from the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) and Lloyd’s Register with virtual mentorship and practical field exercises. As part of the programme, participants attended a virtual “Ask the Expert” session on October 21 with Interferry specialists, Joep Bollerman, Francesco Ruisi and Darren Johnston, to discuss international ferry safety standards. This was followed by live condition and safety compliance audits at operational passenger ferry terminals, supervised by Sandra (Okoli) Ubong of ABS and Engr. Frank Fayinto of Lloyd’s Register. During the field exercises, participants applied an eight-step survey methodology covering preparation, onboard assessment and reporting. They were trained to identify safety deficiencies relating to hull integrity, life-saving appliances, fire protection systems and machinery, while applying the 5W+1H principle to ensure evidence-based reporting. The participants also learnt to classify identified risks into immediate, medium-term and low-priority interventions to facilitate timely corrective action. The initiative is supported by the Lagos State Government and the Special Adviser to the Governor on Blue Economy, Mr Oluwadamilola Emmanuel, alongside Interferry Chief Executive Officer, Mike Corrigan, and Ferrysafe Executive Sponsor, Shari Corrigan. With the successful completion of Module 6, the programme is expected to progress to Module 7, titled “Watchkeeping”, scheduled for November 2026. The next phase will further equip participating maritime professionals with competencies in vessel operations, navigational safety and effective watchkeeping practices. LASWA reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening professional standards, improving passenger safety and developing a more efficient, resilient and sustainable water transportation system in Lagos State and across Africa through international collaboration. top.title: Magic Johnson pinpoints why LA Lakers are really better without LeBron James this season
top.description: Photo by Amanda Edwards/Getty Images Los Angeles Lakers legend Magic Johnson has offered his thoughts on the team’s impressive 10-2 record. After beating the Atlanta Hawks, the LA Lakers moved to the top of the Western Conference. They became the first team in the NBA this season to reach 10 wins. After the win, Skip Bayless posted on X, referring to LeBron James, “The Los Angeles Lakers now have the NBA’s best record. No, they do not miss him.” Magic Johnson has now had his say on the Lakers’ improvement, and he believes the team is simply faster and mentally tougher. He posted: “Last year, the Lakers were a slow team that got beat in transition – but not this season. This team is mentally and physically tougher, and that’s why they’re 10-2!” After losing LeBron James in the offseason, the Lakers were able to use his salary to focus on other areas of the team. They have added more depth and their bench appears stronger than it did last season, with Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton among the additions making an impact. Johnson praises JJ Redick Magic Johnson believes LA Lakers head coach JJ Redick deserves the credit for the improvement, despite Luka Doncic’s incredible performances, averaging 39.3 ppg. Johnson says he has seen signs of development from Redick and is pleased with his impact, now in his third season as a head coach. He posted: “The Lakers’ win over the Hawks yesterday showed that JJ Redick has become a great NBA coach. “His in-game switch from man-to-man to a zone defense changed the trajectory of the game, and he’s outstanding at drawing up plays out of timeouts!” The Lakers are next in action against the Milwaukee Bucks. top.title: Mining: Zamfara task force moves to reclaim gold fields
top.description: The Zamfara State Government inaugurated a 13-man committee to curb illegal mining activities across the state. The Secretary to the Zamfara State Government, Abubakar Mohammad Nakwada, inaugurated the committee on Friday in Gusau, the state capital. This was contained in a statement signed by Mr Sulaiman Tudu, the Senior Special Assistant on Media, Office of the Secretary to the State Government, issued in Gusau on Saturday. The committee, headed by the State’s Commissioner for Environment, Abdulrahman Tumbido, has broad membership across security agencies, traditional institutions, and relevant federal and state government agencies. Inaugurating the committee, Mr Nakwada said the initiative was part of the state government’s efforts to assist the Federal Government in formalising the mining sector in the state. The SSG charged the committee to work closely with security agencies and relevant regulatory and local authorities to identify locations where illegal mining is taking place and profile the operators. The committee will also ensure that even licensed companies comply with relevant laws and regulations, take adequate measures to prevent environmental degradation, and safeguard the safety and rights of host communities. In his remarks, the Chairman of the Committee, Tumbido, said the committee will work with reliable information, respect for the law, fairness and regard for the rights and livelihoods of the people. He added that the committee will ensure that its efforts contribute to lasting security, environmental protection and sustainable development in the state. top.description: CHAPEL HILL, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 02: Matt Able #3 of the North Carolina Tar Heels attempts a free throw during the second half of the game against the Western Carolina Catamounts at Dean E. Smith Center on November 02, 2026 in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The North Carolina Tar Heels are just moments away from facing off against Wyoming in their third game of the regular season. Both teams are going into this one 2-0, and the winner will earn the right to claim a 3-0 record going into this weekend’s slate of matchups. The loser will still be 2-1, but that record would mean very different things depending on which team owns said L. The name of the game for Michael Malone and his team tonight is taking a couple of steps forward without taking any steps backwards. While that sounds like a lazy take based off a statement made by UNC’s head coach, this is also based off observations made from the last couple of games. The great news is that the game against Wofford was more or less what fans needed to see in just about every aspect of the game, and even better, there weren’t many negatives when keeping everything in context. Were they perfect? Of course not. Were they struggling to rebound at times? Sure, but for the most part they improved more than they went backwards, so we’ll see how things pan out tonight. One thing that Carolina fans should bear in mind going into this one is that while this is a mid-major team, Wyoming has been playing really well so far this season. It’s reasonable to think that they will get steamrolled because UNC has way more talent than them, and while the talent aspect may be true, the Cowboys are still more than capable of going crazy offensively and dominating the boards. Don’t be surprised if things don’t look great for at least 10 minutes of this game, but pessimistically, the Heels could lose if they don’t show up for all 40 minutes. UNC is talented, but they’re not “40 percent effort and we’ll still win by 30” talented. As always, we’ll be back after the game with post-game analysis and takes. Until then, Go Heels!

top.description: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 8: Kirk Cousins #8 of the Las Vegas Raiders warms up prior to an NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kirk Cousins returns to the Minnesota Vikings —but can this trade save their season? On this bonus episode of The Real Forno Show , host Tyler Forness and producer Dave Stefano examine the quarterback reunion, its third-round draft cost, and the pressure facing Kevin O’Connell. This Vikings 1st & SKOL discussion balances immediate hope with long-term consequences: Minnesota needs competent offense to support a defense playing winning football. Forness doesn’t soften his assessment of the price: “The Vikings got fleeced.” Yet Stefano sees a necessary response to an offense struggling to sustain drives: “He gives us the best chance at winning ballgames.” The Kirk Cousins trade debate centers on familiarity versus desperation. Forness explains that Cousins already understands O’Connell’s system and has established chemistry with Justin Jefferson, making him a logical option after Kyler Murray’s injury and Carson Wentz’s struggles. The hosts argue that Minnesota’s quarterback problems reflect a series of decisions involving J.J. McCarthy, Sam Darnold, and Daniel Jones—not one isolated mistake. Reviewing Cousins’ Raiders production, Forness cites 2,340 passing yards, 20 touchdowns, eight interceptions, and a 97.1 passer rating. Those numbers offer encouragement, but concerns remain about the 38-year-old quarterback’s late-season stamina, an inconsistent running game, and future salary-cap obligations. Forness gives the deal a C+, explaining, “It was a move they had to make,” while maintaining that Minnesota paid too much. His ultimate measuring stick is straightforward: “If you make a playoff run, it’s worth a third round pick.” Key points from the episode: A familiar quarterback, a faster transition: Cousins’ knowledge of the offense and receivers could help Minnesota stabilize without an extensive learning period. Justin Jefferson needs opportunities: The hosts emphasize getting the ball to Minnesota’s star receiver and avoiding further offensive frustration. The defense deserves support: Forness argues that making a move signals belief in a unit that has continued to compete against strong offenses. top.title: What’s the plan for Utah’s goaltending situation?
top.description: Utah Mammoth goaltender Sebastian Cossa (33) watches as a puck slips past him during an NHL game against the Pittsburgh Penguins at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Monday, Oct. 19, 2026. | Kristin Murphy, Deseret News Is there another position in sports as fickle as goaltending? One minute, you’re the solution to the problem. The next, you are the problem. One day, fans are chanting your name, and the next, they’re essentially calling for your head on a platter. Heck, it might be the most hot-and-cold job in the world. Karel Vejmelka has experienced both sides of the coin in the two-and-a-bit seasons he’s played for the Utah Mammoth. He saved the season in Year 1 when Connor Ingram stepped away from hockey for family and health reasons. In Year 2, he was the only goalie the team could consistently rely on. In both seasons, he earned “Veggie” chants on a near-nightly basis at the Delta Center, and his biggest fans started wearing broccoli hats to support him. Now, a little more than a month into Year 3, many of those same fans hope to see him traded. Vejmelka tries to stay positive. “I think so, yeah,” he said in response to the Deseret News’ question of whether he’s playing up to his standard. “I think, of course, I can be even better, but I just do my best every single day to get better every day. “So just need to keep working on it and just, you know, be positive and just keep playing and just be a key player on the ice. Just give us a chance to play and to win the game every single time.” League-wide, save percentages have been down the last few years. More goals equates to more fan excitement so that’s how the league wants it to be, but Vejmelka is on pace to record the lowest save percentage of his career by a wide margin, and he currently has the second-worst goals saved above expected in the NHL, according to MoneyPuck . Even so, the Mammoth are finding ways to win games. “We’re just kind of in the same spot where we (were) last year,” Vejmelka said. “So we have enough points to be in the in the (top) half in the standings, but we just need to keep going and just be even better.” Sebastian Cossa, the rookie goalie whom Utah acquired this summer in one of the biggest trades of the franchise’s brief history, has similar numbers to Vejmelka and a similar outlook on them. “We’re getting most of the results, which has been good. Like, 4-1-1 right now, so I mean, getting wins, which is good,” Cossa said in reference to the team’s record when he is in net. “I think we can clean up a couple areas of the game ... just continue to get experience here and just keep going uphill.” Rather than placing the blame solely on the goalies, the team sees it as a whole-team issue. top.title: Purdue women's soccer sells out Big 10 title game in 45 minutes
top.description: WEST LAFAYETTE — For Purdue soccer , it was win and worry about the logistics after the fact. The Boilermakers did their part, defeating Wisconsin in the Big Ten Tournament semifinals on penalty kicks, meaning Purdue would host Friday's Big Ten Championship by virtue of being the higher seed. The only issue was how trying to create a championship environment home field advantage would work at basketball-crazed Purdue, where the men's basketball team was hosting Ohio the same night. The answer came on Tuesday morning. Purdue sold out its 2,200-seat capacity for Folk Field in 45 minutes, showing how invested fans have become during a season where Purdue has posted a program record for wins and is 16-2-3 on the season. The timing won't allow for fans to see all of both events, but there is at least adequate time to see portions of both or part of one event and all of the other. The Big Ten Championship women's soccer match between Purdue and Michigan State starts at 6 p.m. Friday, Nov. 13. Purdue's men's basketball game versus Ohio tips off at 7 p.m. More: How Purdue soccer uses data to boost performance "This game being sold out, it's just unbelievable," Purdue women's soccer coach Richard Moodie said. "It's exciting for me that we have another home game. We love being at home. We love Folk Field and that environment and the atmosphere that the fans have created." top.title: Raiders trade deadline notes
top.description: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a 3rd round pick (the Vikings’ second in the round) Tuesday. it opens the door for the Raiders play No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza, who general manager John Spytek confirmed Tuesday afternoon will be the starter moving forward. Here are some notes about their deadline decisions: The Raiders, at 4-5, didn’t decide to make it a fire sale. They also didn’t opt to add at the trade deadline either as they have lost five of the last six games after starting 3-0. NFL reporter Jordan Schulz reported that the Raiders did receive recent trade calls on star defensive end Maxx Crosby, but resisted them after a nixed trade with the Baltimore Ravens in March. Because the Raiders have already agreed to trade Crosby once, expect them to receive more calls in the future, including next offseason. There is no word if the Raiders had any interest in pending free agents, wide receiver Tre Tucker and safety Jeremy Chinn. It will be interesting to see if they try to extend them in the offseason. Spytek said he received calls on multiple players without getting into detail. Despite needs at some posts, including at wide receiver and defensive tackle, the Raiders did not add at the deadline. Spytek said the Cousins’ trade is not an indication the team is giving up on the season. Coach Klint Kubiak said Mendoza is prepared, physically and mentally, for this task and he praised Cousin for his influence on the rookie. Spytek said Mendoza has passed every test since being drafted and he helped the Raiders make the tough decision to deal Cousins. Spytek said Mendoza’s play in practice was difficult to ignore. Spytek said he only received calls on Cousins and did not make any himself. The talks with Minnesota emerged Tuesday morning after Carson Wentz’s horrible showing in a loss Monday night. nigeria.title: LASWA, Interferry complete ferry safety inspection training
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Waterways Authority (LASWA), in partnership with global trade association Interferry, has concluded Module 6 of the Africa Ferry Safety Development and Mentoring Programme to strengthen safety standards across the waterways sector. The training equipped maritime professionals with technical skills to audit and inspect commercial passenger ferries as part of efforts to improve passenger safety and compliance with international maritime standards. The module, titled “Survey and Inspection”, combined self-paced theoretical lessons from the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) and Lloyd’s Register with virtual mentorship and practical field exercises. As part of the programme, participants attended a virtual “Ask the Expert” session on October 21 with Interferry specialists, Joep Bollerman, Francesco Ruisi and Darren Johnston, to discuss international ferry safety standards. This was followed by live condition and safety compliance audits at operational passenger ferry terminals, supervised by Sandra (Okoli) Ubong of ABS and Engr. Frank Fayinto of Lloyd’s Register. During the field exercises, participants applied an eight-step survey methodology covering preparation, onboard assessment and reporting. They were trained to identify safety deficiencies relating to hull integrity, life-saving appliances, fire protection systems and machinery, while applying the 5W+1H principle to ensure evidence-based reporting. The participants also learnt to classify identified risks into immediate, medium-term and low-priority interventions to facilitate timely corrective action. The initiative is supported by the Lagos State Government and the Special Adviser to the Governor on Blue Economy, Mr Oluwadamilola Emmanuel, alongside Interferry Chief Executive Officer, Mike Corrigan, and Ferrysafe Executive Sponsor, Shari Corrigan. With the successful completion of Module 6, the programme is expected to progress to Module 7, titled “Watchkeeping”, scheduled for November 2026. The next phase will further equip participating maritime professionals with competencies in vessel operations, navigational safety and effective watchkeeping practices. LASWA reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening professional standards, improving passenger safety and developing a more efficient, resilient and sustainable water transportation system in Lagos State and across Africa through international collaboration. While commercial operations are picking up in some states, others continue to lag behind. For example, the Anambra State Government had to forcefully shut down markets in Onitsha and other areas to compel traders to reopen on Mondays, yet many businesses still remained closed. The exact reason for this hesitation remains unclear, as the threat of the sit-at-home order has significantly receded across the region, with the violent attacks and harassment of the past now seldom witnessed. However, findings indicate that many South-East residents have simply grown accustomed to this forced Monday routine after experiencing it for so long. Consequently, many individuals—particularly independent business owners—now voluntarily choose to rest on Mondays. Furthermore, several rural communities have permanently adopted Mondays for communal meetings, neighbourhood policing, road repairs, and other civic activities. Ultimately, what began as a forced restriction has largely transitioned into a voluntary day of rest, effectively extending the weekend by an extra day.In Aba, Abia State, following disruptions associated with the Monday sit-at-home, major markets in the commercial city are yet to fully recover their usual Monday patronage. Although Aba, the economic honey-pot of Abia State, is gradually emerging from the disruption associated with the sit-at-home era, investigations have revealed that the psychological and political sentiments that sustained Monday closures continue to influence trading patterns in some parts of the city. nigeria.title: Kebbi APC reconciles aggrieved members ahead of 2027 polls
nigeria.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kebbi State has declared that it is united and strong ahead of the 2027 general elections, following a reconciliation exercise aimed at addressing grievances among party members. The Secretary of the Contact and Reconciliation Committee set up by Governor Nasir Idris, Engineer Ahmed Umar Faruk, made this known on Tuesday in Birnin Kebbi while briefing journalists on the committee’s activities. Faruk said the committee had completed 10 days of engagements across the state’s 21 local government areas, during which it met with aggrieved party members and resolved several complaints. He said those engaged included former commissioners, former members of the state House of Assembly and National Assembly, as well as other party members who felt sidelined or had grievances arising from the concluded party primaries. According to him, the committee recorded significant progress by providing a platform for aggrieved members to express their concerns and ensuring that their complaints received attention. He said the exercise had helped restore unity within the party, adding that the APC leadership in the state was committed to carrying every member along in its activities. “We toured the 21 local government areas in Kebbi State and saw loyalty to the governor and the party from top to bottom,” he said. Faruk urged party leaders at the state, local government and ward levels to sustain regular engagement with members to prevent grievances from accumulating and threatening party unity. He, however, warned members against engaging in anti-party activities and clandestine meetings capable of creating divisions within the APC. He said the party would not tolerate actions capable of undermining its unity as it prepares for the 2027 general elections. The former Anambra governor said he worked with a former Minister of Environment to develop the erosion-control programme, which he said was subsequently adopted following his intervention with the late President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua. “On what the president said while campaigning in Akwa Ibom, it’s not true. Explaining his visit to Plateau State, Obi said it was part of his approach to engaging citizens and understanding their challenges before embarking on campaign rallies. nigeria.title: Makinde Presents ₦1.115tn 2027 Budget To Oyo Assembly
nigeria.description: Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has presented a proposed budget of ₦1.115 trillion for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly for consideration and approval. Tagged the “Budget of Sustained Progress”, the proposal is valued at ₦1,115,341,378,359.90. Presenting the budget on Tuesday at the Assembly complex in Agodi, Ibadan, Makinde said it was designed to consolidate the gains of his administration and lay a foundation for sustainable development beyond its tenure. He described it as the final budget proposal of his administration, saying it would sustain the state’s development momentum and ensure continuity after the transition to a new government. “As we prepare to hand over the baton to the next administration, we bring before you the 2027 Budget of Sustained Progress. It is designed to consolidate our gains, sustain public services and carry our state’s development forward through the transition period and beyond,” he said. The governor said the proposal prioritised infrastructure, community development and the strengthening of public institutions, with significant allocations for capital projects in health, education and road infrastructure. He added that his administration was committed to leaving behind clear records, properly documented processes and institutions capable of sustaining efficient service delivery. Highlighting his administration’s achievements, Makinde said Oyo State’s Internally Generated Revenue increased by 288 per cent, from ₦26.59 billion in 2019 to ₦103.25 billion in 2025. He also noted that the state ranked third nationally in the 2025 Subnational Ease of Doing Business Assessment. world.title: Teddy Riner candidacy 'illustrative of this hunger for an alternative' to Le Pen or Mélenchon
world.description: As Teddy Riner throws his hat in the race for the French presidency, amid France's sociopolitical and economic crises. François Picard is pleased to welcome Lex Paulson, Director of Executive Programs at UM6P School of Collective Intelligence at at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University. The prospect of Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner entering France's presidential race raises questions that extend well beyond the political ambitions of a celebrated athlete. At a time when traditional parties are struggling to mobilize voters and the political center remains deeply fragmented, Riner's emergence points to a broader transformation in democratic competition: the growing importance of personal credibility, public visibility and the capacity to embody an alternative to established political elites. In an interview with France 24, Lex Paulson, Professor of Collective Intelligence at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, argues that the changing relationship between voters and political institutions is reshaping the conditions under which political outsiders can emerge. "The currency of politics now is no longer just money to buy television advertisements or open offices. It's the ability to capture attention." For Paulson, Riner's celebrity status gives him a considerable advantage in an increasingly fragmented media environment. Yet visibility alone does not confer political credibility. While the Olympic champion's public commitments against racism and xenophobia may resonate with voters, Paulson questions whether he has articulated a sufficiently developed political vision to become a serious presidential contender. The deeper issue, however, is not whether Riner can win. It is what his potential candidacy reveals about the weakness of France's traditional political alternatives and the growing demand for leaders whose personal histories, values and commitments resonate with citizens. "Voters don't vote for policies. Voters vote for people they sense will stand up for them." Paulson's analysis connects this demand for political identification to a wider crisis of democratic representation. Voters, he suggests, increasingly perceive professional politicians as a distant governing class that listens to citizens only during electoral campaigns. "People don't feel like they're being listened to except for the few weeks before an election." Seen in this light, Riner's emergence is less an isolated celebrity phenomenon than a symptom of the changing relationship between political authority, public trust and democratic participation. The central challenge facing France's next generation of leaders may therefore be not simply to develop compelling policies, but to restore citizens' sense that political institutions are responsive to their lives. As Paulson concludes, the real political opportunity lies in reimagining governance itself: bringing decision-making closer to citizens and giving them a more meaningful voice in the democratic process.

This is very convenient for anyone who has no electrical hook up. It started with a bet in 2025. Michael Diederich, the owner, began accepting bitcoin for hot tubs after a wager with his brother. Payments were slow to trickle in at first, but bitcoiners kept asking him to build a hot tub powered by bitcoin miners. He started building one, pairing the tub with miners that heat the water. Snorkel works with Dane Soja of Hashrate House on the build . The prototype with two S19J Pro miners drawing about 8 kW, which it says heated a tub from cold to 104°F (40°C) in under four hours. The project won an innovation award at the Heat Punk Summit in Denver , and a Snorkel tub is on display in Denver. Diederich sees a future where every electric hot tub is heated by miners, because the mining income helps pay back the cost of energy that would otherwise be wasted as heat. The Rose Gift House and Coffee, Renton The Rose sits at 226 Main Ave S in downtown Renton, in the Old Renton Pub building. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine LNbits Releases 1.7.0 Urgent Security Update After November 8 Attacks Drain Funds LNbits, the open-source Lightning Network wallet and accounts platform, released version 1.7.0 on November 10 as an urgent security update and instructed all operators to upgrade before restarting their servers. The project’s official X account posted the announcement with a link to the GitHub release , calling it a “SECURITY UPDATE”. The release follows a wave of attacks that began over the weekend. On November 8, LNbits posted on X that all users should stop their LNbits servers immediately after reporting active attacks, adding that security patches were being prepared and that it was “better to err on the side of caution.” The project also disabled instances on its hosted service. Multiple reports documented unauthorized account creation and fund withdrawals. Kevin Ravensberg , operator of the Telegram tipping service BitTipBot, publicly stated that attackers created new accounts on his instance and withdrew 2,285,545 satoshis (approximately 0.0229 BTC) between roughly 09:22 and 14:00 UTC on November 8. According to the official upgrade guidance published alongside the release, versions prior to 1.7.0 are affected and “funds running on prior versions of LNbits are at risk of being stolen.” The project stated that 1.7.0 includes security fixes in response to the incident discovered on November 8 and that a full technical report on the exploit will follow. Operators are advised to set up a fresh server if compromise is suspected, because updating alone cannot remove access an attacker may already have gained. Additional recovery steps include rotating all user wallet keys as Super Admin, replacing funding-source credentials (API keys or macaroons), rotating other secrets stored in settings, and reviewing or re-creating connections for extensions such as NWC Provider, LNDHub, Bolt Cards, TPOS, Bleskomat, and FOSSA. The GitHub release notes describe extensive security hardening across authentication, extension management, and payment handling, plus dependency updates. New features shipping with the version include on-chain wallet support, BOLT12 offer payments, TOTP two-factor authentication, NIP-17 support, a job scheduler, automatic extension updates, and hold invoice support for the LNbits funding source. The project notes that LNbits functions as a hot wallet and that operators should keep only operational balances online, regularly review activity, and move excess funds to offline keys. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Texas Rep. Files Bill Letting Cities Invest $10 Million in Bitcoin A Texas lawmaker filed a bill Monday that would let each city and county in the state invest up to $10 million of public money in bitcoin or another cryptocurrency, without setting any rules for how those coins would be held. House Bill 815, filed by Rep. Ron Reynolds, a Missouri City Democrat, on the first day of prefiling for the 90th Texas Legislature, carries the caption “Relating to the authority of a municipality or county to invest money in cryptocurrencies.” The introduced text , posted on the Texas Legislature’s site, is two sections long. The bill would amend the Public Funds Investment Act, Chapter 2256 of the Texas Government Code, by adding a new Section 2256.0165, titled “Authorized Investments: Cryptocurrency.” Under that section, “a municipality or county may invest not more than $10 million of its money or money under its control in Bitcoin or another cryptocurrency.” The authority would take effect Sept. 1, 2027, if the bill becomes law. The $10 million figure is a cap on each city or county, not a single statewide pool. School districts and other local governments covered by the investment act are left out. What the bill does and does not say The measure borrows its definitions of “Bitcoin” and “cryptocurrency” from Section 403.701 of the Government Code, the definitions written into law last year by Senate Bill 21, which created the Texas Strategic Bitcoin Reserve . Bitcoin is defined as a decentralized cryptocurrency created by a peer-to-peer network that operates independently of any central authority or bank. Cryptocurrency is defined more broadly as a virtual currency that uses cryptography to secure transactions recorded on a distributed ledger, such as a blockchain. That means a city or county would not be limited to bitcoin. The bill also does not import the reserve law’s requirement that coins bought for the state fund have an average market capitalization of at least $500 billion over the most recent 24-month period, or its provisions on cold storage and qualified custodians. The Public Funds Investment Act already requires local governments to adopt a written investment policy that emphasizes safety of principal and liquidity, and to invest with the care a prudent person would use in managing their own affairs. A city or county would still have to add cryptocurrency to that policy before buying any. The new section itself is silent on custody, on audits specific to digital assets, and on how a loss would be handled. A narrower version of last year’s proposal Reynolds filed a broader measure, House Bill 4258, on March 10, 2025, with Rep. Mihaela Plesa. business.title: Poland’s Parliament Votes 240-202 to Let Officials Freeze Crypto Before Court Review
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Poland’s Parliament Votes 240-202 to Let Officials Freeze Crypto Before Court Review Poland’s lower house of parliament voted 240-202 on Friday to let the interior minister freeze crypto assets, bank accounts and other property of people placed on a national sanctions list, before any court reviews the order. The Sejm, Poland’s lower house, passed the Act on Restrictive Measures at its 68th sitting, with one member abstaining and 17 not voting. The Senate received the bill Monday and has 30 days under Article 121 of the Constitution to adopt, amend or reject it, after which it would go to President Karol Nawrocki. The law, a government bill that also implements European Union sanctions rules, treats crypto assets as financial means that can be frozen, using the definition in the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation. A freeze, as the text defines it, is meant to stop any movement, transfer, use or other change that would let the holder benefit from the assets. The freeze applies only to people and entities the interior minister adds to a public national list, either on the minister’s own initiative or at the request of agencies that include the financial watchdog, the central bank, the financial intelligence unit and the internal security service. Grounds include supporting a country already under EU sanctions, serious human rights abuses, or initiating or financing information manipulation that poses a serious threat to Poland’s national security. A listing on that last ground requires a showing of a real and serious threat to Poland’s interests, borders, security or elections. The bill carves out ordinary journalism, political speech and publishing, unless that activity is a knowing campaign of the kind the law describes. A freeze that starts before a judge weighs in The interior minister’s decision takes effect the day after it is posted in the ministry’s Public Information Bulletin and is immediately enforceable. There is no request to the minister to reconsider. A listed person may file a complaint with an administrative court, but the law says the decision remains in force until a judgment becomes final, and it sets aside the usual rule that would let a court pause a challenged order. The measures also bar making funds or property available to listed persons and can exclude them from public contracts. In some cases, the economy minister may appoint a temporary administrator to sell frozen assets or, under a separate order, take them over for the State Treasury. What the freeze would mean for bitcoin The Poland bill does not target ordinary bitcoin holders in Poland. It reaches crypto assets owned, held or under the control of people and firms on the sanctions list. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. Back in 2020, a little less than four months after the NFL decided to move forward with a regularly scheduled season during the COVID-19 pandemic, Allen, then with the Chargers, took issue with the annual NFL Top 100 list of the league's best players. Specifically, he was incensed that he was placed at No. 77, so much so that he tweeted about it and tagged other players he thought he was better than: Tyreek Hill, Mike Evans and Chris Godwin. "Ok I'm tired of biten my tongue…@cheetah @MikeEvans13_ @chrisgoodwin… (and the list goes on) ARE NOT a better reciever than me! Faster than me…every day of the week but separation..CHILD PLEASE!" Allen wrote . It's not hard to see where Allen's frustrations were coming from as he was ranked No. 38 on the list the year before. He might have been so upset that he forgot to check that he tagged the correct Chris Godwin in his post (he did not). Regardless, Evans replied to the callout. "You tagged the wrong Chris Godwin lol and don't be mad at us we ain't make the rankings or care about em," Evans replied . "I like the confidence but be realistic you not on my level bro." You tagged the wrong Chris Godwin lol and don't be mad at us we ain't make the rankings or care about em. Six years is a long time for people to think about some Twitter beef that lasted all of two posts - and one side even conceding some respect for the other. The name of the game for Michael Malone and his team tonight is taking a couple of steps forward without taking any steps backwards. While that sounds like a lazy take based off a statement made by UNC’s head coach, this is also based off observations made from the last couple of games. The great news is that the game against Wofford was more or less what fans needed to see in just about every aspect of the game, and even better, there weren’t many negatives when keeping everything in context. Were they perfect? Of course not. Were they struggling to rebound at times? Sure, but for the most part they improved more than they went backwards, so we’ll see how things pan out tonight. One thing that Carolina fans should bear in mind going into this one is that while this is a mid-major team, Wyoming has been playing really well so far this season. It’s reasonable to think that they will get steamrolled because UNC has way more talent than them, and while the talent aspect may be true, the Cowboys are still more than capable of going crazy offensively and dominating the boards. Don’t be surprised if things don’t look great for at least 10 minutes of this game, but pessimistically, the Heels could lose if they don’t show up for all 40 minutes. UNC is talented, but they’re not “40 percent effort and we’ll still win by 30” talented. As always, we’ll be back after the game with post-game analysis and takes. Until then, Go Heels!

On this bonus episode of The Real Forno Show , host Tyler Forness and producer Dave Stefano examine the quarterback reunion, its third-round draft cost, and the pressure facing Kevin O’Connell. This Vikings 1st & SKOL discussion balances immediate hope with long-term consequences: Minnesota needs competent offense to support a defense playing winning football. Forness doesn’t soften his assessment of the price: “The Vikings got fleeced.” Yet Stefano sees a necessary response to an offense struggling to sustain drives: “He gives us the best chance at winning ballgames.” The Kirk Cousins trade debate centers on familiarity versus desperation. Forness explains that Cousins already understands O’Connell’s system and has established chemistry with Justin Jefferson, making him a logical option after Kyler Murray’s injury and Carson Wentz’s struggles. His ultimate measuring stick is straightforward: “If you make a playoff run, it’s worth a third round pick.” Key points from the episode: A familiar quarterback, a faster transition: Cousins’ knowledge of the offense and receivers could help Minnesota stabilize without an extensive learning period. sports.title: What’s the plan for Utah’s goaltending situation?
sports.description: Utah Mammoth goaltender Sebastian Cossa (33) watches as a puck slips past him during an NHL game against the Pittsburgh Penguins at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Monday, Oct. 19, 2026. | Kristin Murphy, Deseret News Is there another position in sports as fickle as goaltending? One minute, you’re the solution to the problem. The next, you are the problem. One day, fans are chanting your name, and the next, they’re essentially calling for your head on a platter. Heck, it might be the most hot-and-cold job in the world. Karel Vejmelka has experienced both sides of the coin in the two-and-a-bit seasons he’s played for the Utah Mammoth. He saved the season in Year 1 when Connor Ingram stepped away from hockey for family and health reasons. In Year 2, he was the only goalie the team could consistently rely on. In both seasons, he earned “Veggie” chants on a near-nightly basis at the Delta Center, and his biggest fans started wearing broccoli hats to support him. Now, a little more than a month into Year 3, many of those same fans hope to see him traded. Vejmelka tries to stay positive. “I think so, yeah,” he said in response to the Deseret News’ question of whether he’s playing up to his standard. “I think, of course, I can be even better, but I just do my best every single day to get better every day. “So just need to keep working on it and just, you know, be positive and just keep playing and just be a key player on the ice. Just give us a chance to play and to win the game every single time.” League-wide, save percentages have been down the last few years. More goals equates to more fan excitement so that’s how the league wants it to be, but Vejmelka is on pace to record the lowest save percentage of his career by a wide margin, and he currently has the second-worst goals saved above expected in the NHL, according to MoneyPuck . Even so, the Mammoth are finding ways to win games. “We’re just kind of in the same spot where we (were) last year,” Vejmelka said. “So we have enough points to be in the in the (top) half in the standings, but we just need to keep going and just be even better.” Sebastian Cossa, the rookie goalie whom Utah acquired this summer in one of the biggest trades of the franchise’s brief history, has similar numbers to Vejmelka and a similar outlook on them. “We’re getting most of the results, which has been good. Here are some notes about their deadline decisions: The Raiders, at 4-5, didn’t decide to make it a fire sale. They also didn’t opt to add at the trade deadline either as they have lost five of the last six games after starting 3-0. NFL reporter Jordan Schulz reported that the Raiders did receive recent trade calls on star defensive end Maxx Crosby, but resisted them after a nixed trade with the Baltimore Ravens in March. Because the Raiders have already agreed to trade Crosby once, expect them to receive more calls in the future, including next offseason. Spytek said he received calls on multiple players without getting into detail. Despite needs at some posts, including at wide receiver and defensive tackle, the Raiders did not add at the deadline. Spytek said the Cousins’ trade is not an indication the team is giving up on the season. Coach Klint Kubiak said Mendoza is prepared, physically and mentally, for this task and he praised Cousin for his influence on the rookie. Spytek said Mendoza has passed every test since being drafted and he helped the Raiders make the tough decision to deal Cousins. Spytek said Mendoza’s play in practice was difficult to ignore. Spytek said he only received calls on Cousins and did not make any himself. The talks with Minnesota emerged Tuesday morning after Carson Wentz’s horrible showing in a loss Monday night. technology.title: To thwart reverse engineering by agents, dev proposes blinding them
technology.description: Now that LLMs can help analyze commercial software binaries and recreate their functionality, one software developer and student has created a project designed to make this process more difficult. Timo Zhang's project is called Blind LLM Agents (BLA), and as its name suggests, it attempts to interfere with efforts by AI agents to scrutinize app code. "Coding agents can reverse-engineer shipped packages, CLIs, and WASM in minutes," Zhang told The Register in an email. "Classic obfuscation was built for humans and static tools, not LLMs that reason about meaning. Blind LLM Agents is a protection layer for that threat model." Such agents can also help developers build alternatives to existing commercial software. Last month, Artcraft , a two-person development shop, released seven open-source apps that aim to be replacements for Adobe's commercial apps Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro. Artcraft claims these apps are "clean-room reimplementations" written from scratch in Rust using Anthropic Opus 5.5. Setting aside the question of whether enlisting an AI model to reimplement an app really immunizes the creator from legal risk, those making apps face the possibility that someone will have an LLM probe published app binaries and reconstruct them through reverse engineering. There's in fact a framework for this, Reverse Engineer Anything (REA). Zhang has faced some criticism on social media for creating a limited barrier to copying other people's work (which at this point might simply be the work of another LLM). But not everyone accepts that all publicly accessible binaries should be easily available for review and reuse. BLA cannot prevent committed reverse engineering efforts, but it may add a bit of friction to the process when LLMs are involved. "It doesn't write app code — it hardens what you've already built," Zhang said. "A transform pipeline (plus MCP tools / an agent Skill) applies renaming, lane splitting, seed-derived string encryption, build polymorphism, WASM export renaming, decoys, self-seal integrity checks, and a coverage matrix that won't claim protection it can't prove. Behavior stays equivalent; recovery cost goes up." Zhang said various evaluations like red teaming and CrackMe challenges to recover keys or flags from hardened artifacts show that BLA is effective. "We also drive REA (a reverse-engineering agent) against those builds," he said. "Fail-to-break is the pass. CI tracks defense score, self-verifies integrity coverage, and checks functional equivalence. We raise the cost — we don't claim it is unbreakable." The project website says as much, noting that it raises the effort for analysis and adds decoy code, but doesn't promise protection against traditional interactive reverse engineering tools like Ghidra or Frida. technology.title: What happens to mathematics when AI becomes an oracle?
technology.description: Our modern world runs on math, from social media algorithms, package delivery, and weather prediction to medical imaging and machine learning. The rise of computers helped fuel its dominance, enabling us to work with increasingly large numbers that would otherwise be beyond the capacity of our finite human brains. But with the rise of large language models, AI chatbots, and, soon, quantum computing, so-called "big math" is beginning to outstrip its creators entirely. What that means , and how we might adapt, is the focus of a new book, Big Math: The Hidden Codes That Run Our World , by applied mathematicians Steven Strogatz and Alex Townsend. Strogatz is perhaps best known in his field for his co-authorship of a seminal 1998 paper with Duncan Watts on the collective dynamics of small-world networks. He has also studied chaos theory as applied to physics, the geometry of supercoiled DNA, and the biological collective oscillators, such as swarms of synchronously flashing fireflies and crickets that chirp in unison. In 2005, Strogatz extended his study of synchronicity to the crowds that caused the wobbling of London's Millennium Bridge . An award-winning communicator, Strogatz wrote three series of columns on mathematics for The New York Times in 2010, 2012, and 2025 and hosted a podcast for Quanta magazine from 2020–2021. He has written four popular books: Sync (2003), The Calculus of Friendship (2009), The Joy of X (2012), and the New York Times bestseller Infinite Powers (2019). Read full article Comments

science.title: SpaceX moves Starship Flight 15 booster to launch pad for 'squeeze test' ahead of epic double-catch attempt (photos)
science.description: null SpaceX is one big step closer to the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket. The company announced today (Nov. 10) that it had moved its latest Starship first stage, known as Super Heavy Booster 22, to the launch mount at its Starbase facility in South Texas ahead of Flight 15, which is scheduled to lift off this Friday (Nov. 13). During the upcoming launch test, SpaceX plans to catch both Booster 22 and Starship's Ship upper stage with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms in a double landing catch — something the private spaceflight company has never tried before. It will be the first full recovery of an orbital rocket in history. SpaceX's Flight 15 Starship Super Heavy booster in its assembly bay, before its move to Starbase's launch mount. (Image credit: SpaceX) Booster 22 therefore "was used for final catch testing upon arrival [at the pad], including a suspended squeeze test at catch height," SpaceX said in an X post today (Nov. 10). That post shared four photos of the giant booster, which is powered by 33 of SpaceX's next-gen Raptor engines. The first shot showed Super Heavy in one of Starbase's "Mega Bay" assembly buildings before rollout, while the other three depicted it grasped by the tower's arms, held high in the South Texas sky. SpaceX will try to catch both Super Heavy and Ship during Flight 15 — something it's never done before. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has used the chopstick arms during Starship flights before; it has successfully caught Super Heavy on three separate occasions. But the company has never attempted a catch of Ship, which flies higher and farther than the booster and is therefore a more challenging target. And SpaceX only reached orbit with Starship for the first time on Flight 14, which launched on Sept. 28. So Flight 15 will break new ground. And, if all goes to plan, it will give us a look at the future: SpaceX plans to catch Super Heavy and Ship on all operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will allow the company to boost the megarocket's launch cadence. And SpaceX wants to fly Starship incredibly often, so that it can build out its Starlink V3 broadband constellation and even bigger Starmind AI data-center network . Indeed, Elon Musk has said the company is eyeing 10,000 Starship flights per year by 2030. The launch tower's "chopstick" arms giving the Flight 15 Super Heavy a loving squeeze. (Image credit: SpaceX) If all goes to plan, Flight 15 will launch from Starbase on Friday during a 75-minute window that opens at 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT; 4:45 p.m. local Texas time). Super Heavy will return to Starbase for its catch about 6.5 minutes after liftoff. Ship will follow suit much later — about 22 hours later, in fact, after it has deployed 26 Starlink V3 spacecraft into LEO and completed 14 circuits of our planet. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 10, 2013: Europe's GOCE satellite, the 'Ferrari of space,' fell out of orbit after mapping Earth's gravity field
science.description: null On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. GOCE, its name was short for Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer, launched in 2009 on a mission to map Earth's gravity like never before. But despite that successful mission, it was doomed in 2013 when it ran out of fuel . At the time, controllers weren't sure where GOCE would fall back to Earth . Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage. It disintegrated about 50 miles above the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected. It showed small variations in Earth's gravity , mapped the structure of Earth's crust and mantle, and tracked ocean currents. Artist's rendering of the "Ferrari of space," the European Space Agency's Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer (GOCE), before it fell from space in 2013. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Why it mattered The GOCE satellite was a sleek spacecraft, with fins covered in solar panels that gave it a futuristic design. In fact, its look earned it a pretty cool nickname. "GOCE's sleek, elegant aerodynamic design — responsible for it being dubbed the 'Ferrari of space' — immediately set it apart from most other satellites,." ESA officials said in a description . There was more than looks behind GOCE's design. In order to generate the best map ever of Earth's gravitational field, GOCE had to fly in an orbit so low — just 139 miles (224 kilometers) — it needed to counteract the drag from the gossamer thin atmosphere of Earth at that altitude. The International Space Station orbits Earth at nearly twice that altitude. GOCE was powered by an xenon ion engine that allowed to maintain its low orbit for four years. Once it ran out of fuel, the 1-ton satellite could not maintain its position in space , leading to a fiery plunge to Earth. The large size of GOCE — it weighed 2,425 pounds (1,100 kilograms) and was 17 feet (5.3 meters) long and 3.2 feet (1 m) wide — made its reentry stand out, particularly since at least 25% of the satellite was expected to reach the Earth's surface . science.title: A distant exoplanet mysteriously vanished from sight. Astronomers just discovered why
science.description: null Astronomers have solved the mystery of an extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, that "disappeared" after seven years of observations. New research suggests that the planet hasn't vanished at all, but has been dragged off its orbit by an unseen planet. The exoplanet , designated TOI-2535 b, is located around 1,000 light-years away. TOI-2535 b was routinely observed with NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite ( TESS ) space telescope for seven years between April 2019 and March 2026 as it completed its 8.25-Earth day orbit of its parent star. That's 10 times quicker than the orbit of Mercury around the sun and means this blisteringly hot planet is classed as a " hot Jupiter ." However, something strange happened started to happen as astronomers observed the distant world. The orbits of the planet weren't regular like those of other planets, with TOI-2535 b often arriving six hours early or six hours later than when astronomers expected. Then, in March this year, TESS was no longer spotting the characteristic drops in starlight that TOI-2535 b caused as it crossed, or "transited," the face of its parent star. It seemed to have vanished. This team used TESS data to determine that TOI-2535 b is being pulled on by an unseen neighbor and is, in turn, pulling on that planet as well. This is causing the orbits of both worlds in the TOI-2535 system to "wobble." TOI-2535 b disappeared when that wobble tilted it out of alignment with its star. "We think of the universe as resembling clockwork, where everything is regular, but that's not true. If there are multiple planets in a system, they can affect each other's orbits. We know of a few systems that are like this," team member Samuel Yee of the University of California, Los Angeles, said in a statement . "This is the most extreme example we've seen because the two planets are interacting so strongly. The planet's orbit is tilting so quickly that its transit disappeared while we were watching." TOI-2535 b isn't expected to transit its parent star for at least 30 years, but the hidden neighbor tugging on it may cross the face of the star sooner than that. In the meantime, scientists will attempt to decode what this extreme wobbling exoplanet system says about how it formed. Hot Jupiters should be cool customers There is currently a lot of speculation about how hot Jupiter planets like TOI-2535 b form. That is because current routes of planet formation suggest planets like this would need to form around a great deal of ice. Obviously, ice isn't likely to be abundant as close to a star as TOI-2535 b is currently. This means that hot Jupiters likely form far from their stars and then migrate inwards . There are two ways that this could happen. The planet could be excited into an elliptical orbit by violent events like a near-collision with another planetary object, and then interactions with the star pull the planet inwards. Alternatively, the hot Jupiter may be pulled inwards along with the other planets

science.title: Uranus has a weird magnetic field that's stumped scientists for 40 years — we may finally know why
science.description: The posided magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune may stem from extreme conditions lying within their deep interior. Unravelling the mystery behind the magnetic fields of these worlds is giving us new insight into the little-known interiors of the ice giants. Only one spacecraft has ever visited Uranus and Neptune, the Voyager 2 spacecraft which spend past Uranus in January 1986 and Neptune in August 1989. Voyager 2 found that their planetary magnetic fields were, to put it bluntly, wonky. Uranus’ magnetic field was offset from its rotational axis by 59 degrees and isn’t even centered on the planet’s core, but instead is only two-thirds of the way down. Neptune is similar, with a disordered magnetic field offset by 47 degrees and centered halfway between the core and its visible cloud tops. If we compare these planets to Earth , which has a stable magnetic field tilted by just 11 degrees to our planet’s rotation, we can see how extreme the magnetic fields of the ice giants are. Various explanations for the strange magnetic fields of the ice giants have been put forward over the years. Uranus as a whole is tilted by 97 degrees and effectively rolls around the sun , and speculation is that billions of years ago it was knocked on its side by a collision with a long-lost Earth-sized planet. Could this collision have also skewed its magnetic field? This might be a plausible explanation were Neptune’s magnetic field also not similarly skewed without having experienced a collision. Clearly, whatever the cause, it must be intrinsic to the nature of the two ice giant planets. Now, a new study by scientists in the U.S. and the UK, based on computer simulations and Voyager 2’s measurements of the two planets’ magnetic fields, may have found a solution. The solution to the weird magnetic fields of the solar system's ice giants may come down to how planets generate their magnetic field through the dynamo effect. This arises from the swirling, convective motion of an electrically conducting liquid within a rotating body, which is able to generate and maintain a powerful magnetic field. Inside Earth, the electrically conducting fluid is the molten iron in the outer part of our planet’s core, and the magnetic field that it generates has clear north and south poles – what we call a dipole, a phenomenon that we can also see in the two magnetic poles of a simple bar magnet. However, the conditions inside Uranus and Neptune are somewhat different. As ice giants, they contain a lot of volatiles – ammonia, hydrogen, helium, methane, and water surrounding a probable rocky core. Furthermore, Uranus and Neptune are substantially larger than Earth , with 14.5 and 17 times the mass of our planet, respectively. This increased mass creates crushing conditions within the interior of the ice giants. In the final weeks of 1960, two young radio enthusiasts were monitoring transmissions from a home-built listening station on a rooftop in Turin, Italy, when the brothers detected something extraordinary: a faint signal that bore the hallmarks of one originating from space. That wasn't the only surprising thing about the alleged signal:, the transmission carried a very familiar message: it was Morse code for the international distress signal SOS. As the youths listened, the signal seemed to grow weaker. This raised a troubling possibility: could it be that the signal's source was moving farther away from Earth ? And if so, was it possible that this concerning signal was of Soviet origin — perhaps a spacecraft drifting helplessly into space, carrying a cosmonaut on board whose doomed mission had never been publicly acknowledged? These strange events from November 1960 became the first in a series of alleged radio signal interceptions that would form the basis of an enduring Cold War-era mystery involving so-called "lost cosmonauts" — early Soviet space travelers rumored to have died during secret spaceflight missions before Yuri Gagarin's historic flight the following spring, in April 1961.Today, more than six decades later, the story remains one of the most haunting legends of the Space Age. Were there truly early Soviet space missions — with tragically ill-fated cosmonaut crews — that remain undisclosed to this day? science.description: 5 min read NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets — worlds beyond our solar system — throughout our galaxy. Watch to learn how the presence of a planet modifies the gravitational wave signal from tightly orbiting white dwarfs. The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory could detect a Jupiter-mass planet in such systems up to thousands of light-years away. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center Download high-resolution video from NASA’s Scientific Visualization Studio “The most common source for LISA is expected to be double white dwarf systems, which are binaries composed of white dwarfs in tight orbits,” said Casey McGrath, a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County and NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland. “If an exoplanet also orbits within one of these systems, its presence becomes imprinted on the gravitational wave signal in a way we’ll be able to uncover.” Two papers published Tuesday in The Astrophysical Journal detail the findings. The first , authored solely by McGrath, examines the detection method and determines the planet masses and orbital periods where it would work best. The second paper , by McGrath and coauthors, investigates how such planets could be confirmed using NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope . The possibility of detecting exoplanets around LISA double white dwarf systems was first proposed by Japanese astronomer Naoki Seto in 2008. Led by ESA (European Space Agency), the LISA mission is slated for launch in the mid-2030s. As a collaborative partner, NASA is contributing the telescopes, other critical hardware, and engineering and scientific support as part of its mission to better understand how the universe works. The LISA detection method is similar to one called radial velocity that uses light and is already employed to find exoplanets around nearby stars. As a planet orbits, its gravity tugs on its host star, imparting a small reflex motion, or wobble, onto it. This wobble causes the star’s spectrum to oscillate, with spectral lines shifting from redder wavelengths as the star moves away from us to bluer ones as the star moves toward us. The shift is due to a phenomenon called the Doppler effect . “Something similar occurs with gravitational waves,” said Scott Noble, a theoretical astrophysicist at NASA Goddard and a coauthor on the confirmation paper. “By themselves, double white dwarfs will emit gravitational waves at a nearly continuous frequency. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS) NASA's Curiosity Mars rover is sizing up its next dig site on the Red Planet. The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of the Mars site, informally named "Nazca," as thoroughly as possible before drilling into it. What is it? Curiosity snapped the close-up image on Oct. 18, 2026, using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI). The image shows multiple roughly disk-shaped potential crystal formations at the rover's next drill target. MAHLI is located on the turret at the end of the rover's robotic arm. It uses an onboard focusing process to make a composite of images of the same target acquired at different positions to focus on multiple features in a single image. Why is it incredible? Scientists theorize that the "discs and needles" texture takes its characteristic shape as crystals, or "crystal forms," grow. The relatively large sizes of the crystal forms at "Nazca" may provide clues about the temperatures at which they grew, as well as information about the abundance of salts and fluids in the area at the time. Complicating this picture, however, is the fact that mineral crystals can be replaced by other minerals after their original crystallization. The new minerals are known as "pseudomorphs," because they have the same shape as the original minerals but not the same composition or molecular structure. The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of Nazca — which shares its name with an ancient South American civilization that's famous for the large designs it etched into the rock and dirt — before drilling begins. The NASA researchers will then be able to compare the deeper composition to the surface-level composition.

Announced a few months after the flagship Seestar S50 Pro and replacing the now-discontinued Seestar S30 , the new Seestar S30 Plus retains its 30mm aperture and compact chassis, but upgrades to four-element apochromatic optics with extra-low dispersion (ED) glass and two 3.7-megapixel cameras. The ZWO Seestar S30 Plus is a new sub-$500 smart telescope with upgraded optics and dual 3.7MP cameras. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) Seestar S30 Plus: was $499 now $474 It has a 1.2-inch (30 mm) aperture, two 3.7 MP cameras and four-element apochromatic optics bundled into a compact build. View Deal Both produce 1,440 x 2,560-pixel images, while a much-improved 43.5-degree wide-angle camera can capture the Milky Way , constellations , star trails and nightscapes. Built-in filters, a mosaic mode and equatorial (EQ) tracking add considerable deep-sky astrophotography potential. For a telescope weighing just 3.64 lbs (1.65 kg), it’s impressive. It easily fits into a camera bag and could happily live on a bookshelf. The Seestar S30 Plus weighs just 3.64 lbs (1.65 kg) and fits in a camera bag easily. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) I’ve already photographed the Andromeda Galaxy (M31) , the Pleiades (M45) , the Dumbbell Nebula (M27) and the North America Nebula (NGC 7000). The results are excellent for such a small instrument, especially when imaging nebulas with its built-in dual-band filter, which helps reduce light pollution. The Seestar app adds new in-app post-processing options, so you don’t have to mess around with any of that — though you can also export everything as lossless FITS files. The S30 Plus also includes a magnetic solar filter, enabling you to indulge in solar photography safely. The North America Nebula (NGC 7000), the Pleiades (M45) and a star trail imaged using the Seestar S30 Plus. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) With Dwarflab’s $1,299 Draco (3.5-inch/90mm aperture) recently landed in stores and Vaonis’ own $4,990 Atlas (3.1-inch/80mm aperture) not available until 2027, ZWO’s decision to offer an upgraded entry-level smart telescope that buyers can get their hands on right now looks particularly smart. The Andromeda Galaxy (M31) photographed using the Seestar S30 Plus. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) With ZWO's pattern of delivering cheaper smart telescopes without sacrificing on quality, the Seestar S30 Plus could be one of Christmas 2026’s best gifts for anyone interested in astronomy — and maybe that’s the point of it. Either way, first impressions are good. A full review is coming tomorrow, so check back at Space.com to find out our full thoughts and testing.

science.title: A science fiction novel has finally won the Booker prize. It’s about time
science.description: M. John Harrison is considered the first bona fide science fiction author to win the Booker prize Kirsty Wigglesworth/AP/Alamy Back in June, our science fiction columnist Emily H. Wilson made a bold claim : M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything was not only “the best science-fiction book of the year so far”, but also a “wholly original… work of genius”. Not only has Emily been proved right, but perhaps she didn’t go quite far enough. This story of an alien invasion won the Booker prize last night, making it – in the Booker judges’ opinion, at least – not just the best science fiction book of the year so far, but the best novel in any genre of the year. Read more These two new sci-fi novels really impressed us It’s about time. Back in 2009, the great Kim Stanley Robinson – another writer of genius, in my opinion – wrote a piece for New Scientist in which he argued that “three or four of the last 10 Booker prizes should have gone to science fiction novels the juries hadn’t read”. With remarkable prescience, Robinson even tipped Harrison’s Signs of Life as one of those books. Advertisement There has been a long-running reluctance in the literary world to allow science fiction (often abbreviated to SF) into the starry ranks of so-called “literary” fiction. As Harrison himself told the BBC’s Front Row last month, he has “been working for 40 to 50 years to shift the balance, both as a novelist and as a critic… Why shouldn’t a well written SF be considered to be literary fiction?”. His win is being trumpeted today as the first time a science fiction novel has won the Booker prize. I’d quibble a little with that – how about Margaret Atwood’s The Testaments , the sequel to The Handmaid’s Tale , set in a dystopian version of the US, which was 2019’s winner? She’d likely quibble with me in return: Atwood has a lot to say about the difference between science fiction and speculative fiction, defining her Gilead stories firmly as the latter. Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter But this very unwillingness to define a novel as science fiction speaks to that long-running literary snobbery. As the late, great Ursula K. Le Guin put it, reviewing Atwood’s The Year of the Flood back in 2009: “She doesn’t want the literary bigots to shove her into the literary ghetto.” Whether or not Harrison is the first science fiction author to win the Booker, it’s definitely the case that, as Booker Prize Foundation chief executive Gaby Wood put it in the prize announcement: “Many past Booker Prize authors have borrowed facets of science fiction in their work, but M. John Harrison is the first Booker winner to have emerged from the bona fide SF world.” And this means, I hope, that our days of looking down on science fiction are over.
